text:
rafa: hey team, i'm oncall lead for my first rotation next week. a few onboarding Qs: who will be my incident-commander buddy for the first two incidents, where are the "single-page" runbooks for IC duties, and how do i run a pager test that verifies my service-account token (i'm worried about the token scoping we discussed in onboarding)
jin: welcome rafa :wave: i'll be your IC buddy for week1. we'll pair on first two incidents and i'll walk through playbook decisions. add me on PD (jin@redwood.com).
harper: single-page IC runbooks live at https://docs.redwood.com/runbooks/oncall/ic-cheatsheet. it covers incident roles, slack message templates, and a quick checklist for taking and handing off IC.
rafa: thanks. for the service-account token test, is there a safer test than the generic curl? don't want to create noise in monitoring.
jin: good call. use the scoped token test endpoint that validates your IAM scopes without triggering alerts:
```
curl -X POST https://ops-api.redwood.internal/v1/pager/validate_token -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN' -d '{"user":"rafa","scopes":["pager:trigger","sre:read"]}'
```
that returns 200 + a validation id and will not trigger an actual alert. if you see 403 it's missing scope.
rafa: ran validate_token and got 403. my token was minted during onboarding workshop.
harper: 403 here usually means the token was minted with the wrong rolebinding (workshop tokens are ephemeral). jin, can you check the token grant for rafa? also check ~/.redwood/credentials for the token source.
jin: checked  rafa was assigned the "oncall-read" role but not the "pager:trigger" role. just updated RBAC and synced. please re-run.
opsbot: OpsBot: Token validation request received for rafa. queued validation; result: pending sync.
rafa: re-ran validate_token and got 200 with id val-2024-07-01-03. thanks. now, small question: when i'm IC, what's the expected cadence for slack incident updates? is every 5 or 10 minutes preferred?
sre-lead: ICs should post a concise update every 10 minutes for P1s, and every 30 minutes for lower severities. use the template in the IC cheatsheet: "[HH:MM UTC] Summary - Impact - Mitigation - Next update ETA". keep it short.
rafa: perfect. also, how to mark myself as "away" in PagerDuty if i need to step out during a shift? don't want escalations to hit me while i'm away.
jin: set a temporary override in PD: People -> User -> Add Override -> Select replacement and time window. If you need to step out urgently DM the replacement and then set override.
rafa: last Q: for region-specific outages (APAC edge), who do we page first? i assume different owners than US infra?
harper: yes  if the incident affects APAC edge, page the regional-oncall (edge-apac) first, then region infra. global infra only if it's global. the IC cheatsheet has the region routing table.
opsbot: OpsBot: For non-alerting token validation use /validate_token (no alerts). For real pager test use /pager/test which will create a simulated alert. See https://docs.redwood.com/oncall/access-troubleshoot for 401/403 guidance.
rafa: ran a real simulated pager test after validation and got the push. PD shows source: ops-sim and device: android. tried one small runbook edit earlier 94 is it okay for ICs to make minor clarifying edits to runbooks during a live incident?
sre-lead: small editorial fixes (typo, clearer step) are fine, but do NOT change mitigation steps or escalation paths during a live incident. If you need to change a procedure, note it and propose after the incident for a post-incident runbook update.
rafa: copy that. thanks everyone  i'll join the shadow pairing and the learning lab tomorrow. less anxious now :thumbsup:
